出会い、デート、告白、そして相手の家族へ。蓮と苏晴の物語で、気持ちをまっすぐ伝え: Meeting, dating, confessing your feelings and meeting the family. Learn Chinese for saying what you feel straight from the heart, through the story of Ren and Su Qing.
広州で働いて二年の佐々木さんは、同僚の小美の誕生日パーティーに招かれた。土曜の夜: Ren Sasaki, who has been working in Guangzhou for two years, has been invited to his coworker Xiaomei's birthday party. It's Saturday night, and about ten of Xiaomei's friends are at a rooftop restaurant. Things have calmed down a little after the cake was cut, and when Ren goes to get a drink, a girl with short hair comes up beside him.
小美の大学時代の友達、二十六歳。広州の出版社で編集の仕事をしている。好奇心旺盛で: Xiaomei's friend from university, 26. Works as an editor at a publishing house in Guangzhou. Endlessly curious and laughs a lot
広州の日系メーカーで働く日本人、二十八歳。中国語は日常会話に困らないレベル、写真: A Japanese man working for a Japanese manufacturer in Guangzhou, 28. His Chinese is good enough for everyday conversation, and photography is his hobby
共通の友達のパーティーで初めて会った同世代の二人。中国の若者同士なので最初から「: Two people of the same generation meeting for the first time at a mutual friend's party. As young Chinese people do, they use 「你」 from the start and speak casually. Even on first meeting, it's natural to joke around, and if you're interested, to suggest the next get-together yourself. If you're too indirect, your feelings won't come across.
こんにちは。あなたも小美の友達？: Hi, are you a friend of Xiaomei's too?
うん、同僚なんだ。佐々木蓮です。日本人です。: Yeah, we're coworkers. I'm Ren Sasaki. I'm Japanese.
中国語では「々」は使わず、「佐佐木」と漢字を繰り返して書きます。読みは Zuǒz: Chinese doesn't use the Japanese repetition mark 「々」; the character is simply written twice: 「佐佐木」. It's read 「Zuǒzuǒmù」. Japanese names are hard for Chinese people to remember, so just giving your first name, 「莲」, is one option.
私は苏晴。晴れの日の「晴」だよ。: I'm Su Qing. "Qing" as in "sunny day."
中国では自己紹介のとき「晴天的晴」のように、どの漢字かを説明するのが普通です。同: In China, when introducing yourself, it's normal to explain which character your name uses, as in 「晴天的晴」, because so many characters share the same sound. If you can say 「莲花的莲」 (lian as in lotus flower) for yourself too, people will remember you right away.
すてきな名前だね。僕は蓮の花の「蓮」。: What a pretty name. Mine is "lian" as in lotus flower.
中国語すごく上手だね。中国に来てどれくらい？: Your Chinese is really good. How long have you been in China?
二年かな。来たばかりの頃は「你好」すらちゃんと言えなかったよ。: Two years. When I first came, I couldn't even say "「你好」" properly.
「连〜都…」は「〜さえも…」。自分の失敗談を少し大げさに話すと、場が和んで相手も: 「连...都...」 means "even...." Telling your own blunders with a bit of exaggeration lightens the mood and makes it easier for the other person to talk. Lots of young Chinese people love self-deprecating jokes and humor.
「真的假的？」は「マジで？」にあたる、若者の定番リアクション。本当に疑っているの: 「真的假的？」 is a go-to reaction among young people, like "For real?" or "No way!" She doesn't actually doubt him; it shows surprise and interest.
本当だって！ 初めて出前を頼んだとき、「辛くしないで」のつもりが「激辛で」って言: It's true! The first time I ordered takeout, I meant to say "not spicy" and said "extra spicy" instead.
あはは、それで食べたの？: Ha ha ha, so did you eat it?
食べたよ。辛すぎて涙が出た。: I did. It was so spicy it made me cry.
「辣得我眼泪都出来了」は「辛くて涙まで出た」。「形容詞 + 得 + 結果」で、ど: 「辣得我眼泪都出来了」 means "it was so spicy it even brought tears to my eyes." "Adjective + 「得」 + result" vividly describes how bad something was. In romance, you'll also hear things like 「想得睡不着」 (missing someone so much you can't sleep).
かわいすぎでしょ。そうだ、普段は何するのが好き？: That's way too cute. Oh, by the way, what do you usually like to do?
写真が好きで、週末はよく古い街並みに撮りに行くんだ。: I like taking photos. On weekends I often go shooting in the old streets.
ほんと？ 私も好き！ すごくきれいで、しかも人が少ない場所知ってるよ。: Really? Me too! I know a spot that's especially gorgeous, and there are hardly any people there.
じゃあ……今度、連れて行ってくれない？: So... would you take me there sometime?
興味のある相手には、具体的な理由（写真）をきっかけに次の約束をつくるのが自然です: With someone you're interested in, it's natural to use a concrete reason (photography) as a hook for the next meeting. 「你可以带我去吗？」 is a more modest invitation than 「下次一起去吧」, since it hands the lead to the other person, and it won't be awkward even if they say no.
いいよ。WeChat交換しよう、またそのとき連絡するね。: Sure. Let's add each other on WeChat, and we'll be in touch.
「我们是同事」＝同僚です。「同学」はクラスメート: 「我们是同事」 = "We're coworkers." 「同学」 means classmate
w:好听|（音・名前が）きれいだ、耳に心地よい: pleasant-sounding; nice (of a sound or name)
名前を褒めるときの定番。「好看」は見た目がきれい: The standard word for complimenting a name. 「好看」 means good-looking
「在中国待了两年」＝中国に二年いる。ここでは dāi と読む: 「在中国待了两年」 = to have been in China for two years. Read 「dāi」 here
「连你好都说不好」＝「你好」さえ言えなかった: 「连你好都说不好」 = couldn't even say 「你好」 properly
驚きを表す若者言葉。疑っているわけではない: Slang among young people expressing surprise. It doesn't mean they doubt you
「外卖」はデリバリー。美团などのアプリで頼むのが日常: 「外卖」 means delivery. Ordering through apps like Meituan is part of everyday life
「眼泪都出来了」＝涙まで出た。笑いすぎ、辛すぎのときにも: 「眼泪都出来了」 = even brought tears to my eyes. Also used when laughing too hard or eating something too spicy
人の言動や性格にも使う。男性に使ってもほめ言葉: Also used for someone's actions or personality. Even for a man, it's a compliment
「你平时喜欢做什么？」＝普段は何をするのが好き？ 趣味を聞く定番: 「你平时喜欢做什么？」 = "What do you usually like to do?" The standard way to ask about hobbies
「给我拍张照」＝写真を撮って。デートの定番アクティビティ: 「给我拍张照」 = "Take a picture of me." A classic date activity
広州の「西关」など、昔ながらの通り。写真好きに人気: Traditional streets such as Guangzhou's Xiguan (「西关」). Popular with photographers
「带我去」＝連れて行って。誘いの口実に便利な言葉: 「带我去」 = "Take me there." A handy word for creating an excuse to ask someone out
w:联系|連絡する: to contact; to get in touch
「到时候联系」＝そのとき連絡するね: 「到时候联系」 = "We'll be in touch then"
日本語の「愛人」とは全く違う同形異義語。恋人は「男朋友」「女朋友」: A false friend: the characters look like "love + person," but it doesn't mean a lover (in Japanese, the same characters mean a secret lover). A boyfriend or girlfriend is 「男朋友」 or 「女朋友」
いちばん簡単なこと（または意外なこと）を例に出して、程度を強調する形。自分の失敗: A pattern that emphasizes degree by giving the simplest (or most surprising) thing as an example. It's often used when telling stories about your own blunders, and exaggerating a little can get a laugh. In romance, it's also used when you're touched by someone's thoughtfulness, as in 「他连我的生日都记得」 (he even remembered my birthday).
来たばかりの頃は「你好」さえ言えなかった。: When I first came, I couldn't even say "「你好」" properly.
彼は私の好きな飲み物まで覚えていた。: He even remembered what I like to drink.
忙しくてご飯を食べる時間さえなかった。: I was so busy I didn't even have time to eat.
どれくらいの程度だったかを、結果で具体的に描く表現。「很辣」と言うより「辣得我眼: An expression that paints the degree of something concretely through its result. 「辣得我眼泪都出来了」 lets people picture the scene and makes the story funnier than just saying 「很辣」. It can also be used to express feelings, as in 「高兴得睡不着」 (so happy I can't sleep).
辛すぎて涙が出た。: It was so spicy it made me cry.
うれしくて眠れない。: I'm so happy I can't sleep.
相手の得意なことや知っている場所をきっかけに、次に会う約束をつくる誘い方。「一起: A way of asking someone out that uses something they're good at, or a place they know, to set up the next meeting. It's more modest than 「一起去吧」 and puts the other person in the role of guide, so it flatters them a little while asking for a date naturally. Another plus is that it's light enough to laugh off if they say no.
今度連れて行ってくれない？: Would you take me there sometime?
あなたのいちばん好きなお店に連れて行ってくれる？: Would you take me to your favorite restaurant?
週末、古い街並みを案内してくれる？: Could you show me around the old streets this weekend?
友達の紹介、パーティー、趣味のイベントなど、自然な出会いの場面。名前の漢字の説明: Natural ways of meeting people, like introductions through friends, parties and hobby events. The flow of explaining the characters in your name, telling a small story about a blunder, finding a shared hobby and then making plans can be used not only in romance but also for making friends.
日本的に「もしよかったら、いつか、機会があれば……」と遠回しにしすぎると、興味が: Being too indirect, like "If it's OK with you, maybe someday, if there's a chance...," tends to make people think you're not interested. On the other hand, abruptly asking 「你有男朋友吗？」 the first time you meet will put people on guard. Get closer bit by bit through common topics.
中国の女性は、相手が自分の話に興味を持って質問してくれるか、ユーモアがあるかをよ: Chinese women pay close attention to whether a guy is interested in what they say and asks questions, and whether he has a sense of humor. Seeing someone trying hard to joke in a foreign language is enough on its own to leave a good impression: "This guy is genuine and fun."
中国の恋愛は日本よりストレートです。好意があれば早めにWeChatを交換し、すぐ: Dating in China is more direct than in many places. If you like someone, you swap WeChat early and make the next plan right away. Messaging each other every day is normal too. Expecting the other person to read between the lines tends to be taken in China as "maybe he's not interested," so put your feelings into words. Being direct, though, is not the same as being pushy. If someone says 「到时候联系」, don't rush, but don't forget to get in touch either. Remember what they said about that photo spot. That kind of sincerity builds trust. People who can turn their mistakes into laughs are attractive in any country.
中国語の「爱人」の意味は？: What does 「爱人」 mean in Chinese?
片思いの相手: Someone you have a one-sided crush on
中国語の「爱人」は夫や妻のこと。恋人は「男朋友」「女朋友」と言います。日本語とは: In Chinese, 「爱人」 means a husband or wife. A boyfriend or girlfriend is 「男朋友」 or 「女朋友」. Despite the characters, it doesn't mean a lover (in Japanese, the same characters mean something completely different).
自己紹介で「我叫苏晴，晴天的晴」と言うのはなぜ？: Why does she say 「我叫苏晴，晴天的晴」 when introducing herself?
天気の話をしたいから: Because she wants to talk about the weather
同じ発音の漢字が多いので、どの字か説明するため: Because many characters share the same sound, so she's explaining which one
晴れの日に生まれたから: Because she was born on a sunny day
中国語は同音の漢字が多いため、自己紹介で漢字を説明するのが一般的です。: Chinese has many characters with the same sound, so it's common to explain the characters when introducing yourself.
「真的假的？」と言われたら、相手はどんな気持ち？: If someone says 「真的假的？」, how are they feeling?
話を終わらせたい: They want to end the conversation.
「真的假的？」は「マジで？」にあたるリアクション。驚きや興味の表れです。: 「真的假的？」 is a reaction like "For real?" It shows surprise and interest.
気になる相手を自然に次の約束に誘うには？: How can you naturally invite someone you like to meet again?
共通の話題をきっかけに、相手に案内を任せる形で誘うのが自然。遠回しすぎても、いき: It's natural to use a shared topic as a hook and invite them in a way that lets them be the guide. Being too indirect or too abrupt won't work.
